Export of herbal and
medicinal plants
*101. MISS MABEL REBELLO:
SHRI B. J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Export-Import Bank of
India has identified herbal and medicinal
plants as an important sub-sector for
enhancement of exports;
(b) whether the current global demand
of the herbal and medicinal plants is around
51,000 crores and whether it has released
a booklet in this regard; and
(c) Government's action plan for
exploiting the situation to the maximum
in the global market?
Dual fees proposal for CAS
*102. SHRI SURESH KALMADI:
Will the Minister of INFORMATION
AND BROADCASTING be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Cable
Operators have rejected Government's
price and dual-fees proposal for the
Conditional Access System (CAS);
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps taken by Government to
get their cooperation?
CGHS dispensary in NOIDA
*103. SHRI DARA SINGH
CHAUHAN: Will the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there is
only one CGHS dispensary in NOIDA
(U.P.);
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
number of Central Government employees
residing in NOIDA has increased manifold
in the recent past;
(c) whether Government are also aware
that about 20,000 beneficiaries are residing
in Sector 62, NOIDA alone;
(d) if so, whether Government propose
to open a CGHS dispensary in that sector;
and
(e) if so, by when and if not, the reasons
therefor?

Setting up of Broadcasting Regulatory
Authority of India
*104. SHRIMATI BIMBA RAIKAR:
SHRI NANA DESHMUKH:
Will the Minister of INFORMATION
AND BROADCASTING be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government propose to set
up a Broadcasting Regulatory Authority of
India on the lines of TRAI;
(b) if so, whether Government have
examined functioning of such other
regulatory bodies like Federal
Communications Commission of US and
Office of the Communications of UK
before taking a view in this regard; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Reforms in DDA
†*105. SHRI LAJPAT RAI:
SHRI RAJIV RANJAN
SINGH 'LALAN':
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Delhi
Development Authority (DDA) has
assigned a professional institution with the
task of providing suggestions regarding
comprehensive reforms in its policy,
working and structure; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
name of the institution and by when it
would submit its report to DDA?
Exploitation of children
†*106. DR. PRABHA THAKUR: Will
the Minister of SOCIAL JUSTICE AND
EMPOWERMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware of
the fact that thousands of innocent children
are being used for begging;
(b) whether Government are also aware
that a number of children are compelled to
beg at the age when they should be getting
education; and
(c) if so, the steps taken by Government
for helping such children to get rid of such
exploitation, giving details of children
rehabilitated in the last two years?
Private partnership in drinking water
sector
*107. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT AND POVERTY
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that five global
corporates are ready to tap over $ 2000 million
market of drinking water in the country;
(b) whether Government have
encouraged the private partnership in the
drinking water sector; and
(c) whether it is a fact that if
privatisation of drinking water is allowed,
the urban dwellers would have to pay at
least ten times more for drinking water?
Janani Suraksha Yojana
*108. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO:
SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that in order to
tackle the problem of maternal mortality
Government have started a new programme
called "Janani Suraksha Yojana";

States under the Centrally Sponsored

Tribal Affairs; Urban Development and Poverty Alleviation)
Total number of questions—155
Mangalore as SEZ
717. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
include Mangalore as Special Economic
Zone for the speedy economic and
industrial development;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the  reasons therefor?
Ban on outsourcing services from
India
718. SHRI  R. P. GOENKA: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a)  whether any steps have been taken
to pursuade the U.S. Administration
against the  reported attempts by States
like New Jersey and others in the U.S. to
legislate a ban on outsourcing certain
services from India, which is likely to
adversely affect the IT and IT enabled
services (ITES) industries in the country
because of their sheer dependence on the
U.S.  market; and
(b) if so, the details thereof, especially
outcome  of the recent meetings with the
U.S. trade representatives in Washington,
where this subject matter  was also
reported to have come up for discussion?
Co-ordination between India and
China for Doha Development
Round of WTO
719. SHRI  SURESH PACHOURI:
Will the  Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether India and China would
engage themselves in a co-ordinated
manner on the issues of common interest
in the ongoing negotiations of the Doha
Development Round of WTO;
(b) if so, the issues/areas identified for
this purpose; and
(c) how the 'Anti-dumping' issue is
proposed to be solved?
Expansion of list of duty free imports
by U.S.A.
720. SHRI  VAYALAR RAVI: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether U.S. President has
expanded the list of imports from
developing countries that can enter U.S.
duty free;

158
WIN2\SESSION\1752RS 158
(b) whether a major hurdle has cropped
up in the way of India's Rs. 1,000 crore
carpet exports to U .S. as this key product
has been deleted from the list of the items
eligible for duty free import into U.S.;
(c) whether a number of countries have
gained by this decision;
(d) if so, to what extent it would be a
loss to India;
(e) whether this issue has been taken
up with the U.S. Government; and
(f) if so, what is their reaction?
Fresh tariff concessions to China
721. DR.  M. N. DAS: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether India has offered fresh
tariff concessions to China on a number
of items as part of the strategy to boost
the trade ties;
(b) if so, whether after the agreement
reached with China, Government have
decided to have 10 year excise relief for
new units in Sikkim and new units
engaged in 13 specified industrial
activities and commencing production on
or after December 23, 2002 in Sikkim
would be entitled to a 10 year excise
exemption; and
(c) if so, to what extent this would give
a boost to the trade between the two
countries?
Trade between Japan and India
722. DR. A.R. KIDWAI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
 Will the  Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether trade between Japan and
India is at a very low stage at present;
(b) if so, whether it has been suggested
that the current complementary structure
of trade should shift to more value-added
and diversified products;
(c) whether 200 Japanese firms are
operating in India and are prepared to
increase their investments provided the
operating environment improves;
(d) if so, to what extent India has
considered these suggestions and has
modified the rules for more Japanese
investments in the country;
(e) whether Japan has welcomed this
move; and
(f) if so, to what extent it would be
further improved?
Visit of Pakistani business
delegation
723. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
SHRI K. RAHMAN KHAN:
SHRI K. NATWAR SINGH:
Will the  Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Pakistani businessmen
visited India in June-July, 2003 and two-
day meeting between Indian and Pakistani
businessmen was inaugurated by the
External Affairs Minister;
(b) whether India and Pakistan have
decided to open up trade channels;
(c) whether India and Pakistan have
entered into tea accord and Pakistan has
decided to import 10-15 million kg. of tea
from India;
(d) if so, whether Pakistani traders
urged the Prime Minister to relax visa
norms for businessmen and submitted
joint memorandum for normalisation of
trade relations; and
(e) if so, to what extent this would help
improving trade relations between the two
countries?
